name: Kallady Bridge
facts: Built in 1924, the Kallady Bridge was the oldest and longest iron bridge in Sri Lanka, spanning the Batticaloa Lagoon as part of the historic A4 Colombo-Batticaloa highway.
Named Lady Manning Bridge after the wife of Governor William Manning, it once saw an average of 10,000 vehicles daily on its single narrow lane, making accidents a major traffic headache.
In 2013, a new 288.35‑meter, two‑lane bridge opened beside the original, costing Rs. 2.6 billion and funded by a JICA loan under the Pro‑Poor Eastern Infrastructure Development Project.
